figures.shows: Two panels (a) H2O and (b) LiH. y: energy error versus FCI in Hartree (log scale, about 1e-4 to 1e-1); x: iterations 0 to 40. Series: ADAPT-VQE with 10k shots (green dots with error bars) and noiseless ADAPT-VQE (red line); a shaded band marks chemical accuracy. The noiseless curve falls into the chemical accuracy band (at about iteration 15 for H2O and about iteration 8 for LiH) and keeps falling; the 10k-shot curve stays above the band, near about 5e-3 to 1e-2 for H2O and about 1e-2 for LiH.
figures.confirmed_by: On the other hand, introducing measurement noise immediately reduces the quality of the ADAPT-VQE output, and the algorithm stagnates well-above the chemical accuracy threshold of 1 milliHartree despite a moderate number of iterations.

figures.shows: Two panels (a) H2O and (b) LiH. y: energy error versus FCI in Hartree (log scale, about 1e-4 to 1e-1); x: iterations 0 to 40. Series: ADAPT-VQE 10k shots (green), GGA-VQE 5k shots (blue, error bars), ADAPT-VQE noiseless (red), GGA-VQE noiseless (black dash-dot), chemical accuracy band. The GGA-VQE 5k-shot curve lies below the ADAPT-VQE 10k-shot curve for most iterations in both panels (about 3e-3 against about 5e-3 for H2O near iteration 30; about 2e-3 to 3e-3 against about 1e-2 for LiH). Both noiseless curves fall below the chemical accuracy band.
figures.confirmed_by: Thus, in the case of the H2O molecule, GGA-VQE is nearly twice as accurate as ADAPT-VQE after about 30 iterations.

figures.shows: Stretched linear H6 chain, 3 Angstrom. y: energy error versus FCI in Hartree (log scale, about 0.03 to 1); x: iterations 0 to 70. Series: ADAPT-VQE 10k shots (green), GGA-VQE 5k shots (blue), GGA-VQE with reoptimisation (red). All start near about 0.7. GGA-VQE (blue) flattens at about 0.14 from about iteration 10. ADAPT-VQE (green) declines slowly to about 0.05 by about iteration 60. GGA-VQE with reoptimisation (red) drops to about 0.07 by about iteration 12, then declines to about 0.05 by iteration 70. Error bars are large.
figures.confirmed_by: As Figure 3 indicates, the post-processed GGA-VQE algorithm yields essentially the same accuracy after a dozen iterations as the ADAPT-VQE algorithm does after nearly 30 iterations.

figures.shows: y: variational energy in eV (about -13.0 to -12.3); x: iterations 0 to about 37. Series: emulator reference curve (blue line), hybrid energy evaluation (green crosses), QPU energy evaluation (orange with error bars), exact ground state energy (red dashed line at about -12.98). The emulator and hybrid curves fall from about -12.5 at iteration 0 to about -12.95 near iteration 25 and then plateau. The raw QPU energies stay between about -12.6 and about -12.3, with no clear downward trend after about iteration 10.
figures.confirmed_by: Figure 4 illustrates the convergence of the hybrid energy evaluations of the GGA-VQE ansatz wave-function with respect to the number of algorithm iterations.

figures.shows: Fidelity of the GGA-VQE ansatz (hybrid evaluation) with the exact ground state against iterations. Left: iterations 0 to about 37, fidelity about 0.78 at iteration 0 rising almost linearly to about 0.987 at iteration 24 and then holding at about 0.98 to 0.985. Right: zoom for iterations 20 to 38, fidelity axis 0.95 to 1.00, peak at about 0.987 at iteration 24, then about 0.982 to 0.985 afterwards.
figures.confirmed_by: Indeed, the greedy, gradient-free operator selection procedure that we have introduced in this study, which relies on a function extrapolation using five noisy evaluations on the QPU, is able to build an ansatz with an energy error below 2.50 × 10−2 eV and a fidelity exceeding 98% with the exact ground state (see Figure 5).

figures.shows: Four panels (iterations 1, 10, 23, 24). y: expected energy drop in eV (0 to about -0.025); x: operator from the pool, numbered 1 to 48. At iteration 1, bars of about -0.017 to -0.025 eV appear for the operators numbered about 25 to 48 (the ZiYi+1 operators) and none for 1 to 24. At iteration 10 the pattern is similar with fewer bars. At iterations 23 and 24 the drops are mostly below about 0.005 eV, with one bar of about -0.016 eV near operator 41 at iteration 23.
figures.confirmed_by: We observe maximal energy drops of approximately 1.5 × 10−2 eV for the first 24 iterations followed by a great reduction in the potential energy drops from iteration 25 onwards.

figures.shows: Schematic: ansatz energy (y) against excitation parameter theta from minus pi to pi (x). papers.what_it_is: A method paper that introduces GGA-VQE, a greedy gradient-free adaptive VQE that fixes each operator and angle in one step from a few circuit measurements, tested on H2O, LiH and stretched H6 with an emulator and on a 25-qubit transverse-field Ising chain on an IonQ Aria QPU.

The paper limits the conclusion to accessible, dynamically correlated molecules (Section 3). Both are entered as new assertions.

assertions.value: The authors state that their algorithm selects, in one shot, both a locally optimal unitary operator and its optimal angle, and does not re-optimise the earlier ansatz (the frozen core), which avoids the global optimisation of a multi-dimensional noisy cost function.

not re-optimising the “frozen-core” of the previous ansatz, we are able to avoid the global optimisation of a multi-dimensional noisy objective function

assertions.value: The authors state that, to the best of their knowledge, their work is the first attempt to combine gradient-free analytical optimisation with energy sorting and develop a greedy gradient-free adaptive variational quantum eigensolver.
quotes: to the best of our knowledge, our work is the first attempt to combine both approaches and develop a greedy gradient-free adaptive variational quantum VQE.
assertions.certainty_reason: A novelty claim by the authors, qualified by their own knowledge.

assertions.value: The authors state that the expectation value of a Hermitian operator with respect to an ansatz parametrised by a single quantum gate is an elementary trigonometric function of the angle, so that for a single rotation gate two measurements at judiciously chosen angles allow exact reconstruction of the full expectation value as a function of the angle.
quotes: Thus, for a wave-function parametrised by a single rotation gate, only two measurements of the expectation value for judiciously chosen values of θ , allow an exact reconstruction of the full expectation value as a parametrised function of θ .
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper presents this as a known result from the fixed-ansatz literature (references 27 to 33).

figures.shows: Flowchart of a quantum simulation algorithm in five purple boxes: identify the system Hamiltonian (fermionic, bosonic, spin, mixed); Hamiltonian encoding (Jordan-Wigner, Bravyi-Kitaev, parity, higher order spin); state preparation (excitation in Fock basis, maximally mixed state, Slater determinant); state evolution and measurement (Suzuki-Trotter, linear combination of unitaries, direct measurement, correlation function, phase estimation, spectroscopic eigenvalue estimation); error mitigation (minimize circuit depth, optimize qubit topology, measurement error mitigation, scaled native gates, post-selection, probabilistic error correction, zero noise extrapolation, Pauli twirling, dynamical decoupling). figures.confirmed_by: Common methods and techniques used in quantum simulation, along with a small subset of representative references, are enumerated below each purple box with bold indicating the processes used for the example model in this work.

figures.shows: Classically computed probability on site 0 (y, 0 to 1) against time (x, 0 to about 13). Series: exact (black solid), m = 5 Trotter steps (blue dash-dot), m = 8 (red dashed).
